---
title: "JQI_PoliticalAttitudes_Taxes"
output: html_document
---

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# POLITICAL ATTITUDE: TAX BURDEN
# ============================================================
#
# tax:
#   1 = Paying too much
#   2 = About right
#   3 = Paying too little
#   4 = Don't pay income taxes -> DROP
#
# Higher values = more favorable assessment of tax burden
#
# Models:
#   M1: Employment status
#   M2: Employment status + social class
#   M3: Employment status + JQI
#   M4: Employment status + social class + JQI
#   M5: Full model
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Construct tax outcome
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_political <- jqi_political %>%
  mutate(
    tax_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(tax)),

    tax = dplyr::case_when(
      tax_num %in% 1:3 ~ tax_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    tax = ordered(
      tax,
      levels = 1:3
    )
  )

write_csv(jqi_political, here("01_tidydata", "GSS_Data_Cleaned", "jqi_politicalattitudesdata.csv"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Run pooled model comparison
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pooled_tax <- run_pooled_model_comparison(
  jqi_political,
  "tax"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Model fit
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pooled_tax$fit


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Likelihood-ratio tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pooled_tax$lr_tests


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Extract tax coefficients
# ------------------------------------------------------------

tax_model_results <- purrr::map2_dfr(
  pooled_tax$models,
  pooled_tax$fit$model,
  function(model, model_name) {

    broom::tidy(model) %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        term %in% c(
          "compensation",
          "benefits",
          "earnings_stability",
          "prestige",
          "log_realrinc"
        )
      ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        model = model_name,
        statistic = estimate / std.error,
        p.value = 2 * pnorm(
          abs(statistic),
          lower.tail = FALSE
        )
      )
  }
)

tax_model_results

pooled_tax$lr_tests

# ============================================================
# UPDATED JQI INCREMENTAL CONTRIBUTION PLOT
# INCLUDING TAX BURDEN
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Add tax to the pooled LR results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pooled_lr_tests_with_tax <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pooled_lr_tests,
  pooled_tax$lr_tests
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Recreate the incremental JQI table including tax
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fit_wide <- pooled_fit %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    model_number = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("^1\\.", model) ~ 1,
      grepl("^2\\.", model) ~ 2,
      grepl("^3\\.", model) ~ 3,
      grepl("^4\\.", model) ~ 4,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(model_number %in% 1:4) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    model_number,
    AIC,
    BIC
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = model_number,
    values_from = c(AIC, BIC),
    names_glue = "{.value}_M{model_number}"
  )


lr_jqi <- pooled_lr_tests_with_tax %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    grepl("M1 vs M3", comparison) |
      grepl("M2 vs M4", comparison)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    comparison_short = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("M1 vs M3", comparison) ~
        "JQI beyond employment status",

      grepl("M2 vs M4", comparison) ~
        "JQI beyond employment status + class"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    comparison_short,
    lr_statistic,
    df,
    p_value
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = comparison_short,
    values_from = c(
      lr_statistic,
      df,
      p_value
    ),
    names_glue = "{.value}_{comparison_short}"
  )


jqi_incremental_table <- fit_wide %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    lr_jqi,
    by = "outcome"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    delta_AIC_M1_M3 = AIC_M3 - AIC_M1,
    delta_BIC_M1_M3 = BIC_M3 - BIC_M1,

    delta_AIC_M2_M4 = AIC_M4 - AIC_M2,
    delta_BIC_M2_M4 = BIC_M4 - BIC_M2
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Prepare plot data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_plot_data <- jqi_incremental_table %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    delta_AIC_M1_M3,
    delta_AIC_M2_M4
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      delta_AIC_M1_M3,
      delta_AIC_M2_M4
    ),
    names_to = "comparison",
    values_to = "delta_AIC"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    # Reverse sign so larger values = greater improvement
    AIC_improvement = -delta_AIC,

    comparison = dplyr::recode(
      comparison,
      delta_AIC_M1_M3 =
        "JQI beyond employment status",
      delta_AIC_M2_M4 =
        "JQI beyond employment status + class"
    ),

    outcome = factor(
      outcome,
      levels = c(
        "eqwlth",
        "tax",
        "kidssol",
        "poleff11",
        "getahead"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "Income inequality",
        "Tax burden",
        "Children's future",
        "Political efficacy",
        "Hard work vs. luck"
      )
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(
  jqi_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = AIC_improvement,
    y = outcome,
    shape = comparison
  )
) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    size = 3
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Improvement in model fit (−ΔAIC)",
    y = NULL,
    shape = NULL,
    title = "Incremental contribution of objective employment quality",
    subtitle =
      "Improvement in fit from adding compensation, benefits, and earnings stability",
    caption =
      "Larger values indicate greater improvement in AIC."
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +

  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  here::here(
    "04_figures",
    "JQI_PoliticalAttitudes.png"
  ),
  width = 12,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300
)
```
